title: t1532: derive MAX_WORKERS_CAP default from total RAM instead of static 8
body:
## Summary

- MAX_WORKERS_CAP defaulted to 8 regardless of machine capability, silently throttling throughput to ~33% on a 64GB machine (8/24 usable slots)

- Explicit user config (`orchestration.max_workers_cap` in settings.json or `MAX_WORKERS_CAP` env var) still takes precedence

## Scaling table

| Total RAM | Default Cap (old) | Default Cap (new) |
|-----------|-------------------|-------------------|
| 8 GB | 8 | 4 |
| 16 GB | 8 | 20 |
| 32 GB | 8 | 32 |
| 64 GB | 8 | 32 |

title: t1507: Receipt/invoice forwarding with phishing protection
body:
## Summary

- Adds `email-receipt-forward-helper.sh` — detects transaction emails, verifies sender DNS (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), forwards verified to accounts@, flags suspicious for manual review
- Adds `tests/test-email-receipt-forward.sh` — 20 tests, all passing

## Pipeline

1. **Detect** transaction email via subject/body pattern matching (receipts, invoices, payment confirmations, order confirmations, subscription renewals, billing statements)
2. **Phishing check** — hard block on URL shorteners, bitcoin/cryptocurrency payment references, urgent wire transfer language — never forwarded
3. **DNS verification** — SPF/DKIM/DMARC scoring (pass threshold: ≥57%). Known legitimate domains (stripe.com, paypal.com, github.com, etc.) bypass DNS-fail hard block but get `[DNS-WARN]` annotation
4. **Forward** verified emails to configurable accounts@ via AWS SES; falls back to `pending-forwards.jsonl` log if SES unavailable
5. **Flag** suspicious emails to `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/email-receipt-forward/flagged/` with JSONL audit log

## Usage

```bash
# Process a single email
email-receipt-forward-helper.sh process ~/Downloads/invoice.eml

# Dry run
email-receipt-forward-helper.sh process ~/Downloads/invoice.eml --dry-run

# Verify a sender domain
email-receipt-forward-helper.sh verify-sender stripe.com

# Scan a mailbox directory
email-receipt-forward-helper.sh scan-mailbox --dir ~/Maildir/INBOX/new/

# Check status
email-receipt-forward-helper.sh status
```

## Config

```bash

# Edit ~/.config/aidevops/email-receipt-forward.json
# Set accounts_email and sender_email
```

title: fix: verify PR is merged before marking task complete
body:
## Summary

- `task-complete-helper.sh` accepted `--pr NNN` and immediately committed the TODO completion without verifying the PR was actually merged
- This caused the premature-completion bug observed in [Ultimate-Multisite/ai-agent#466](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ai-agent/issues/466): t085 was marked complete while PR #465 was still open
- `planning-commit-helper.sh` already had this check (lines 154-173) but `task-complete-helper.sh` — the canonical script — did not

## Changes

- **`verify_pr_merged()`** — new function that calls `gh pr view --json state,mergedAt` and blocks if `state != MERGED` or `mergedAt` is empty/null
- **`--gh-repo <owner/repo>`** — new option for cross-repo PR lookups (when the TODO repo differs from the PR repo)
- **`--skip-merge-check`** — escape hatch for tests/CI only; logs a warning when used
- Uses `jq` for JSON parsing (consistent with the rest of the framework)

The check runs in `main()` after `parse_args`, before `complete_task`, so `TODO.md` is never modified if the PR is not yet merged.

## Behaviour

**Before:** `task-complete-helper.sh t085 --pr 465` would immediately mark t085 complete regardless of PR state.

**After:** The script calls `gh pr view 465 --json state,mergedAt`, checks `state == MERGED` and `mergedAt` is non-null, and exits with an error if not:

```
[ERROR] PR #465 is not merged (state: OPEN)
[ERROR] Task completion is only allowed after the PR is merged.
[ERROR] Wait for the PR to merge, then re-run: task-complete-helper.sh t085 --pr 465
```

## Testing

```bash
# Should fail (PR open/closed but not merged)
task-complete-helper.sh t999 --pr 1 --no-push

# Should succeed (merged PR)
task-complete-helper.sh t999 --pr <merged-pr-number> --no-push

# Cross-repo lookup
task-complete-helper.sh t999 --pr 465 --gh-repo Ultimate-Multisite/ai-agent --no-push

# Skip check (tests only)
task-complete-helper.sh t999 --pr 1 --skip-merge-check --no-push
```

## Root cause reference

Discovered via [Ultimate-Multisite/ai-agent#466](https://github.com/Ultimate-Multisite/ai-agent/issues/466). The fix belongs in the framework (this repo) since `task-complete-helper.sh` is the shared script used by all workers.

title: t5136: Fix pulse-wrapper.sh to use neutral PULSE_DIR, prevent session accumulation
body:
## Summary

- Change `PULSE_DIR` default from `~/Git/aidevops` to `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/` — a neutral path not associated with any managed repo
- Update `setup.sh` launchd plist and cron job to use the neutral workspace path instead of the aidevops repo directory
- Document why session reuse is intentionally disabled for pulse role (stale context prevention from PR #4129)

## Problem

When a repo has `pulse: false` in repos.json, the pulse supervisor still ran FROM that repo's directory (via `PULSE_DIR` default), creating 155+ orphaned "Supervisor Pulse" sessions associated with the wrong project in ~36 hours. Two root causes:

1. **Misleading project association** — `PULSE_DIR` defaulted to `~/Git/aidevops` in both `pulse-wrapper.sh` (line 214) and `setup.sh` (launchd/cron env vars). Sessions were filed under that project even with `pulse: false`.
2. **Session accumulation** — Session reuse was intentionally disabled for pulse role in PR #4129 (`headless-runtime-helper.sh` clears session ID each cycle to prevent stale conversational context from contaminating dispatch decisions). Each cycle creates a fresh session by design.

## Fix

The supervisor is a framework-level process, not a project-level one. Using `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/` as the working directory means pulse sessions are filed under the framework workspace rather than polluting any specific project's session list. Sessions are still created each cycle (by design), but they no longer accumulate under a managed repo.

**Note for existing installations:** Users need to run `aidevops update` (which re-runs `setup.sh`) to regenerate the launchd plist or cron job with the new `PULSE_DIR` value. Until then, the old env var from launchd/cron will override the new default in `pulse-wrapper.sh`.

title: t1541: structural enforcement for self-improvement repo routing
body:
## Summary

- Adds `framework-routing-helper.sh` — a structural enforcement tool that detects framework-level tasks and provides a single action (`log-framework-issue`) to route them to the aidevops repo
- Adds a framework routing guard to `claim-task-id.sh` that warns when a framework-level task is being created in a non-aidevops repo

- Updates `AGENTS.md` and `build.txt` to reference the structural enforcement

## Problem

GH#5149 / GH#2849: Workers under autonomous supervisor dispatch create framework-level tasks in project repos instead of routing to the aidevops repo. The prose-only fix from PR #2850 is insufficient — autonomous workers don't reliably follow multi-step conditional workflows ("if framework → find aidevops path → claim ID there → file issue upstream"). They default to the repo they're running in.

Evidence: tasks t4107 and t9411 were filed in qs-agency despite being framework-level (supervisor pipeline bug, model tier optimization).

## Solution

Implements **Option D + C + A** from the issue's root cause analysis:

**D: `log-framework-issue` as a first-class action** — `framework-routing-helper.sh log-framework-issue` creates issues on the aidevops repo with dedup, source-repo context, and correct slug resolution. Workers don't need to invent the cross-repo workflow — they call one command.

**C: Routing decision prompt step** — The pulse command (`pulse.md`) now includes a "Self-improvement repo routing" section that instructs the supervisor to run `framework-routing-helper.sh is-framework` before creating any self-improvement task, and route accordingly.

**A: Guard in `claim-task-id.sh`** — When claiming a task ID, the script checks if the title references framework-level concerns and the repo is not aidevops. If so, it emits a warning on stderr. This is advisory (never blocks allocation) but visible to callers.

## Detection Logic

`is-framework` uses pattern matching across three categories:
- **Path patterns**: `~/.aidevops/`, `.agents/`, `prompts/build.txt`, etc.
- **Component patterns**: `pulse-wrapper`, `ai-lifecycle`, `supervisor`, `claim-task-id`, `headless-runtime`, etc.
- **Concept patterns**: "cross-repo orchestration", "task routing", "model tier", "pulse logic", etc.

Fixes the recurrence of GH#2849: workers still create framework-level tasks in project repos despite the prose fix in PR #2850. The prose-only fix is insufficient for autonomous workers under supervisor dispatch — they need a first-class action to route framework issues correctly.

Closes #5149

## Root cause

Three failures in the current system (from issue analysis):
1. **Prose-only enforcement**: Workers know the rules but don't execute multi-step conditional workflows reliably under time pressure
2. **No correct action path**: Workers had no first-class action for "this is a framework issue, route to aidevops repo"
3. **`/log-issue-aidevops` not wired in**: Exists for interactive use but not referenced in the supervisor's action menu

## Changes

### New: `framework-issue-helper.sh`

A dedicated script providing three commands:

- **`detect TEXT`** — deterministically identifies framework-level indicators (path patterns, script names, concept keywords). Exit 0 = framework issue, exit 1 = project issue. Catches both documented failure cases from the issue (t4107 "supervisor evaluate/dispatch" and t9411 "ai-lifecycle.sh").
- **`log --title T --body B`** — files an issue directly on `marcusquinn/aidevops` with auto-deduplication. Safe to call multiple times.
- **`check-repo`** — verifies if the current repo is the aidevops framework repo.

### Guard in `claim-task-id.sh`

Non-blocking warning when called from a non-aidevops repo with framework indicators in the title. Surfaces the routing question before the ID is allocated. Suppressible via `SKIP_FRAMEWORK_ROUTING_CHECK=true` for intentional cross-repo use.

### Updated `AGENTS.md` Self-Improvement section

Replaces prose guidance with a concrete action path:

```bash
# Detect if a problem is framework-level
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/framework-issue-helper.sh detect "description"

# File a framework issue (not claim-task-id.sh in the project repo)
~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/framework-issue-helper.sh log \
  --title "Bug: ..." --body "Observed: ..."
```

### Updated `pulse.md`

Adds `log_framework_issue` as a named supervisor action alongside `merge_pr`, `fix_ci`, and `dispatch_worker`. Workers now have a button to press, not just a manual to read.

## Verification

```bash
# Framework indicators correctly detected
bash .agents/scripts/framework-issue-helper.sh detect "Model tier downgrade detection in supervisor evaluate/dispatch"
# → framework (exit 0)

bash .agents/scripts/framework-issue-helper.sh detect "Phase 3 pipeline stdin consumption bug in ai-lifecycle.sh"
# → framework (exit 0)

bash .agents/scripts/framework-issue-helper.sh detect "Fix broken CSS on homepage"
# → project (exit 1)

# check-repo works
bash .agents/scripts/framework-issue-helper.sh check-repo
# → is_aidevops=true (exit 0)

# Deduplication works
bash .agents/scripts/framework-issue-helper.sh log --title "Test framework issue" --dry-run
# → Found existing issue, skipping duplicate
```

## Design notes

- The guard in `claim-task-id.sh` is a **warn, not a block** — workers may have legitimate reasons to allocate IDs in the current repo. The warning surfaces the routing question without breaking existing workflows.
- `framework-issue-helper.sh detect` uses deterministic pattern matching (no LLM call) — fast, cheap, and reliable for the common cases. The patterns cover the two documented failure cases from the issue.
- The `SKIP_FRAMEWORK_ROUTING_CHECK=true` escape hatch prevents the guard from becoming an obstacle for the aidevops repo itself or for intentional cross-repo work.

title: feat: pattern-driven model tier downgrade using historical success data (GH#5148)
body:
## Summary

- Adds `record-tier-downgrade-ok` and `tier-downgrade-check` commands to `pattern-tracker-helper.sh` with a new `TIER_DOWNGRADE_OK` memory type
- Wires `evaluate.sh` to record `TIER_DOWNGRADE_OK` patterns when tasks complete successfully at a cheaper tier than requested (quality_score ≥ 2)
- Wires `headless-runtime-helper.sh` `choose_model()` to check pattern data before dispatch via `AIDEVOPS_TIER_DOWNGRADE_TASK_TYPE` env var

## Design

**Conservative by default** — requires 3+ successes AND zero failures at the lower tier before any downgrade. This addresses the issue owner's concern that "two attempts with Sonnet would cost more than one and done with Opus" — the bar is high enough that only well-proven downgrades are applied.

**Non-blocking** — any failure in the pattern lookup (missing DB, unavailable sqlite3, unknown tier) falls through to the original model. Dispatch never fails due to this feature.

**Monotonic** — only downgrades, never upgrades. Tier rank: haiku=1 < flash=2 < sonnet=3 < pro=4 < opus=5.

**Gradual** — first N tasks run at the AI-classified tier; downgrade kicks in after confirmed successes accumulate.

**Transparent** — logs `"Model for dispatch: pattern data recommends sonnet over opus (TIER_DOWNGRADE_OK, task_type=feature)"` when a downgrade is applied.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `.agents/scripts/archived/pattern-tracker-helper.sh` | Add `record-tier-downgrade-ok`, `tier-downgrade-check` commands |
| `.agents/scripts/supervisor-archived/evaluate.sh` | Record `TIER_DOWNGRADE_OK` on successful cheaper-tier completions |
| `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` | Wire `tier-downgrade-check` into `choose_model()` |
| `.agents/scripts/memory-helper.sh` | Add `TIER_DOWNGRADE_OK` to valid memory types |
| `.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh` | Add `TIER_DOWNGRADE_OK` to `PATTERN_TYPES_SQL` |
| `tests/test-tier-downgrade.sh` | Test suite: 10 pass, 2 skip (deployment-dependent) |

## Usage

```bash
# Dispatch with task type hint (enables pattern-driven downgrade)
AIDEVOPS_TIER_DOWNGRADE_TASK_TYPE=feature headless-runtime-helper.sh run ...

# Manually record a downgrade (called automatically by evaluate.sh)
pattern-tracker-helper.sh record-tier-downgrade-ok \
  --from-tier opus --to-tier sonnet --task-type feature --quality-score 2

# Check if downgrade is supported
lower=$(pattern-tracker-helper.sh tier-downgrade-check \
  --requested-tier opus --task-type feature --min-samples 3)
```

Closes #5148

title: t5161: Fix status:blocked label substring matching in pulse-wrapper
body:
## Summary

- Replace `grep -qF 'status:blocked'` with comma-padded exact pattern matching (`[[ ",${existing_labels}," == *",status:blocked,"* ]]`) to prevent false positives from labels containing `status:blocked` as a substring (e.g., `archive-status:blocked`)
- Uses the standard shell idiom for exact element matching in comma-delimited lists — bash 3.2 compatible, no external process spawned

## Details

**File:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh:2612`
**Root cause:** `grep -qF 'status:blocked'` performs a fixed-string substring search, so any label containing `status:blocked` as a substring would match (e.g., `archive-status:blocked`, `old-status:blocked-v2`).

**Fix:** Pad the comma-delimited label string with commas on both sides and match against `,status:blocked,`. This ensures the match is exact — the label must be a complete element in the list, not a substring of another label.

**Before:** `echo "$existing_labels" | grep -qF 'status:blocked'`
**After:** `[[ ",${existing_labels}," == *",status:blocked,"* ]]`

title: t5197: Fix wp-helper.sh SSH commands silently failing
body:
## Summary

- Replaces broken `bash -c '...' _ args` SSH pattern with `printf '%q'`-escaped single command string
- Fixes all WP-CLI commands over SSH silently failing with exit code 1 and no output
- Affects cloudways, hetzner, cloudron, hostinger, closte hosting types (localwp unaffected)

## Root Cause

SSH concatenates multiple command arguments with spaces into a single string before passing to the remote shell. The `bash -c '...'` pattern passed wp_args as separate SSH arguments, but the remote shell received a flat string where `bash -c`'s script and its positional parameters were merged — causing `shift` to fail (exit 1) and `wp` to never execute.

## Fix

Build the full remote command as a single `printf '%q'`-escaped string and pass it as one argument to SSH. Each wp arg is individually escaped, preventing both injection and argument-boundary loss. Applied to both the key-based SSH path (hetzner/cloudways/cloudron) and the sshpass path (hostinger/closte).

## Validation

Per issue #5197, tested against live Cloudways sites:
- Basic: `wp core version` → `6.9.4`
- Flags: `plugin list --fields=name,version --status=active --format=table` → full table
- Injection: `core version '; echo INJECTED'` → blocked (exit 1, no injection)
- Multi-site: 4 different sites → all correct

Closes #5197

title: GH#5210: Fix duplicate dispatch by adding pre-dispatch open PR existence check
body:
## Summary

- Adds a new dedup layer (`has_open_pr_for_issue()`) that queries GitHub for open PRs matching the task ID or issue number before dispatching a worker
- Integrates as Layer 3 in `check_dispatch_dedup()`, making it a 4-layer dedup system (process match → title key match → **open PR check** → merged PR check)
- Adds standalone `has-open-pr` CLI command to `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` for external use

## Problem

The pulse-wrapper dispatched new workers for tasks that already had an active worker and open PR. The existing dedup only checked local processes (Layer 1-2) and merged PRs (Layer 3), but never checked for **open** PRs on GitHub. A worker that created a PR but whose process had exited (or ran on another machine) was invisible to those layers.

## Solution

Three-strategy open PR search:
1. Issue number in PR title (`#NNN in:title`)
2. Task ID in PR title (`tNNN in:title`, extracted from issue title)
3. Closing keywords in PR body (`closes #NNN in:body`, `fixes #NNN in:body`, `resolves #NNN in:body`)

This is a deterministic check — "does an open PR exist for this issue?" has exactly one correct answer regardless of context.

## Verification

- Tests: 15/15 pass (6 new tests added covering all search strategies + integration)

title: t1543: OAuth multi-account pool plugin for provider credential rotation
body:
## Summary

- Add `oauth-pool.mjs` module to the `opencode-aidevops` plugin enabling multiple Anthropic OAuth accounts with automatic credential rotation on rate limits (429)
- Integrate pool provider registration and `/model-accounts-pool` management tool into the existing plugin
- Uses the same public OAuth client ID and PKCE flow as the built-in `opencode-anthropic-auth` plugin — no fork or upstream dependency needed

Closes #5243

## Problem

OAuth subscriptions (Claude Pro/Max) are significantly cheaper than API keys, but OpenCode stores one credential per provider. Hitting rate limits mid-session means waiting with no recovery. OpenCode PR anomalyco/opencode#11832 proposes this natively but has been open 6+ weeks with no maintainer review.

## Solution

A plugin-layer implementation using the existing OpenCode plugin API:

### New file: `oauth-pool.mjs` (544 lines)

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| PKCE generation | Pure `crypto` — no `@openauthjs/openauth` dependency |
| Pool I/O | Read/write `~/.aidevops/oauth-pool.json` (0600 permissions) |
| Token refresh | Automatic refresh of expired access tokens via Anthropic's token endpoint |
| Account rotation | On 429: mark current account as rate-limited, pick next available (LRU) |
| Request transform | Tool name prefixing, system prompt sanitization, beta headers (matches built-in plugin) |
| Response transform | Strip `mcp_` prefix from streaming tool names |
| Auth hook | Registers `anthropic-pool` provider with OAuth login flow |
| Pool tool | `/model-accounts-pool` for list, remove, status, reset-cooldowns |

### Modified: `index.mjs` (+20/-7 lines)

- Import and wire `oauth-pool.mjs` exports
- Add pool provider registration to config hook
- Add `model-accounts-pool` tool to tool registry
- Add `auth` hook to plugin export
- Destructure `client` from plugin input for token storage

## How to use

**Add an account:**
```
opencode auth login → Select "Anthropic Pool" → Enter email → Authorize in browser → Paste code
```

**Add more accounts:** Repeat the above — each login adds to the pool (doesn't replace).

**Manage accounts:**
- `/model-accounts-pool list` — show all accounts with status
- `/model-accounts-pool remove user@example.com` — remove an account
- `/model-accounts-pool status` — rotation statistics
- `/model-accounts-pool reset-cooldowns` — clear all cooldowns

**Use the pool:** Select any model under the `anthropic-pool` provider in the model picker. Rate limits are handled automatically.

## Testing

- Module syntax check: `node --check oauth-pool.mjs` — passes
- Import verification: all 3 exports resolve correctly

title: GH#5249: Fix chrome-devtools.json validation failure in validate-mcp-integrations.sh
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5249

- Replace fragile `bash -c` + `python3 -m json.tool` JSON validation with direct `jq`/`python3 -c` validation
- Add `validate_json_file()` helper that prefers `jq` (fast, purpose-built) with `python3` fallback using proper `sys.argv` argument passing
- Warn when no JSON validator is available instead of silently failing

## Root Cause

The `run_test()` function passes commands through `bash -c "$test_command"`, introducing double-shell-interpretation. For JSON validation, the command was constructed as:

```bash
run_test "JSON validation: $filename" "python3 -m json.tool '$config_file'"
```

This string goes through two levels of shell expansion. While the quoting is technically correct for simple paths, `python3 -m json.tool` has version-specific behavior differences that caused `chrome-devtools.json` to fail on some systems while other JSON files in the same directory passed. The file itself is valid JSON (confirmed by direct `jq` and `python3 -m json.tool` invocation).

## Fix

Bypass `run_test`'s `bash -c` wrapper entirely for JSON validation. The new `validate_json_file()` function:
1. Uses `jq empty "$file"` (preferred — fast, no quoting issues)
2. Falls back to `python3 -c "import json, sys; json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))" "$file"` (proper argument passing via `sys.argv`, not shell string interpolation)
3. Returns success if no validator is available (skip rather than false-fail)

title: t1545: Enforce issue templates and triage gate for external contributors
body:
## Summary

Closes #5265

- Replace freeform markdown issue templates with YAML forms requiring structured fields (version, OS, AI assistant, error output, reproduction steps)
- Disable blank issues via `config.yml` and direct users to `/log-issue-aidevops`
- Add `issue-triage-gate.yml` GitHub Action that auto-labels external issues `needs-triage`, preventing pipeline pickup without maintainer review
- Update pulse dispatch logic to skip `needs-triage` issues
- Update CONTRIBUTING.md and `/log-issue-aidevops` docs to document the recommended filing path

## Problem

External users (e.g., vRobM's 10 issues on GH#5222-5257) could file issues via the web UI with poor quality reports (raw ANSI escape codes, contradictory information, missing reproduction steps). The pipeline would auto-dispatch workers and merge fixes without any human review — the entire flow from external issue to merged code was fully autonomous with no triage gate.

## How It Works

### Three layers of enforcement:

1. **YAML issue forms** — web users must fill required fields (version, OS, assistant, clean error output, reproduction steps). No more freeform text dumps. Both templates auto-apply `needs-triage` label.

2. **Triage gate workflow** — `issue-triage-gate.yml` runs on `issues.opened`. Checks `authorAssociation`:
   - `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` → bypass triage, remove `needs-triage` label
   - Bot accounts → bypass triage
   - Issues with task ID prefix (`t1234:`) → bypass triage (internal tooling)
   - Everyone else → ensure `needs-triage` label, remove `status:available`/`auto-dispatch`, post welcome comment

3. **Pulse skip rule** — pulse.md updated to never dispatch workers for issues with `needs-triage`. Maintainer must remove the label and add `status:available` to approve.

### Maintainer workflow:

1. External issue arrives with `needs-triage` label
2. Review the issue quality and scope
3. If valid: remove `needs-triage`, add `status:available` → pipeline picks it up
4. If needs info: comment asking for clarification
5. If invalid: close as duplicate/out-of-scope

## Files Changed

- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` — new structured bug report form (replaces `.md`)
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml` — new structured feature request form (replaces `.md`)
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` — disables blank issues, adds `/log-issue-aidevops` link
- `.github/workflows/issue-triage-gate.yml` — auto-labels external issues
- `.agents/scripts/commands/pulse.md` — skip `needs-triage` in dispatch
- `.agents/scripts/commands/log-issue-aidevops.md` — document as recommended path

title: t1548: Add local callback server for OpenAI OAuth redirect
body:
## Summary

- Adds a temporary HTTP server on port 1455 to catch the OpenAI OAuth callback redirect
- The server auto-captures the authorization code and feeds it back to the auth flow
- User just presses Enter in OpenCode after authorizing in the browser — no manual code copying needed
- Falls back to manual paste if the server can't start (port in use)

## Problem

OpenAI's OAuth flow redirects to `http://localhost:1455/auth/callback?code=XXX`. OpenCode's built-in auth spins up a server on that port, but our pool auth hook doesn't. Without a server, the browser shows "connection refused" and the user can't complete the OAuth flow.

## Fix

The `authorize()` function now starts a temporary HTTP server on port 1455 before returning the OAuth URL. When the browser redirects after authorization:

1. Server catches the request, extracts the `code` parameter
2. Shows a success page ("You can close this tab")
3. Resolves a promise with the code
4. The `callback()` function checks for the server-captured code first
5. If the user just presses Enter (empty input), uses the auto-captured code
6. If the user pastes a code manually, uses that instead
7. Server auto-closes after first request or 5-minute timeout

Closes #5318

title: fix: OAuth pool unknown email handling — pending token flow and provider visibility
body:
## Summary

Fixes three related bugs in the OAuth account pool that caused token loss and broken re-auth UX:

- **Unknown email phantom entries**: OpenCode skips plugin-defined `prompts` during re-auth, so `inputs?.email` is always undefined. Previously this created phantom "unknown" entries that couldn't be matched to real accounts. Now `upsertAccount` refuses unknown emails when named accounts exist, and saves tokens to a pending area instead.
- **Pool providers invisible in auth dialog (Ctrl+A)**: Commit 0532f05e7 removed dummy models from pool providers to stop them appearing in the model picker, but this also removed them from the auth dialog entirely (OpenCode requires at least one model entry). Restored dummy model entries.
- **Pending token assignment flow**: New `savePendingToken`/`assignPendingToken` functions persist unidentified tokens in the pool file under `_pending_{provider}`. The MCP tool gains an `assign-pending` action, and `list` shows pending tokens. This prevents token loss when email resolution fails.

Also improved prompt messages to show numbered account lists with clearer re-auth vs new account instructions.

1. Re-authed both Anthropic accounts via the Pool provider
2. Verified "unknown" entry was blocked (not saved to pool)
3. Verified pending token was saved and successfully assigned via `assignPendingToken`
4. Verified both pool providers appear in Ctrl+A dialog after restart
